events.title: Latino Conservation Week 2026
events.description: Get ready for San Diego’s 7th Annual Latino Conservation Week! A week of adventure, community, culture, and conservation is coming your way. Explore the coastal wetlands with Wander the Wetlands and Journey Through the Wetlands, experience the powerful Haagua FILM Screening & PANEL, celebrate our connection to the coast at the Beach Fiesta, and come together for our Latino Conservation Week Celebration. Whether you’re passionate about conservation or simply looking for new ways to enjoy the outdoors, there’s something for everyone. Bring your friends. Bring your family. Bring your love for the outdoors. Join us as we explore, celebrate, connect, and take action! RSVP at the link in bio or at https://bit.ly/LCWSD2026   Spanish ¡Prepárate para la 7.ª Semana Anual de Conservación Latina de San Diego! Se acerca una semana llena de aventura, comunidad, cultura y conservación. Explora los humedales costeros con Wander the Wetlands y Journey Through the Wetlands, disfruta de la poderosa proyección de la película Haagua FILM seguida de un panel, celebra nuestra conexión con la costa en la Beach Fiesta y únete a nuestra Celebración de la Semana de Conservación Latina.   Ya sea que te apasiona la conservación o simplemente buscas nuevas maneras de disfrutar del aire libre, ¡hay algo para todos! Trae a tus amistades. Trae a tu familia. Trae tu amor por la naturaleza.

events.title: Latino Conservation Week: Wander the Wetlands & California Biodiversity Day
events.description: Join San Diego Bird Alliance and our partners for a fun, free, family-friendly morning celebrating the incredible biodiversity of Mission Bay's wetlands! Explore Kendall-Frost Marsh through hands-on activities and learn about the plants, animals, and habitats that make this ecosystem so special. San Diego Coastkeeper will lead a bilingual (English-Spanish) Water Quality Demonstration and provide insight into our latest 2025 Mission Bay Water Quality Report. This bilingual (English/Spanish) community event offers opportunities to connect with nature while contributing to community science during California Biodiversity Day. Activities include: Bird watching walk Fish seining demonstration Invertebrate exploration Native plant walk Nature observations with iNaturalist Water quality talk and demonstration Educational activities for all ages Whether you're an experienced naturalist or visiting the wetlands for the first time, everyone is welcome! Date: Saturday, September 12, 2026 Time: 9:00 AM – 1:00 PM Location: UC San Diego Kendall-Frost Marsh (Crown Point Entrance) Come discover the amazing wildlife of Mission Bay and celebrate Latino Conservation Week and California Biodiversity Day with us! For questions, contact: Kornelas@sandiegobirdalliance.org Bring: Weather-appropriate attire and water Optional: Waterproof shoes and a camera We will meet at the southern end of Crown Point Park, near the dirt lot. Parking: San Diego, CA 92109 Address: Crown Point Dr, San Diego, CA 92109 Coordinates: 32°47'21.2″N 117°13'54.8″W Google Maps Link Register Here! Important Notes: Age: This event is suitable for all ages, though children must be accompanied by an adult. Accessibility: Please be aware that the terrain will include uneven sandy beaches. Expect to travel a short distance from the parking area to the meeting point and navigate uneven terrain, so be prepared for a bit of a trek. Weather Reminder: The event will take place rain or shine, but please check for updates in case of severe weather conditions. Safety: Please stay within the designated areas and respect the natural environment. Why Fish Seining? Fish play a critical role in maintaining the food web; they are an essential food source for many bird species. By monitoring fish populations through activities like fish seining, we can gain insight into the health of the marsh’s aquatic habitats. Healthy fish populations indicate clean, thriving waters, which ultimately benefit the birds that call the marsh home. In essence, by protecting the fish, we are also protecting the birds and the broader ecosystem. So, when you help us with fish seining, you’re not just learning about fish—you’re contributing to the long-term conservation of both the birds and the habitat they rely on. This is a partnership project between UC San Diego Natural Reserve System and San Diego Bird Alliance.
events.location: Kendall Frost Marsh (Crown Point Entrance), Crown Point Dr, San Diego, CA 92109

events.title: Latino Conservation Week “Journey Through the Wetlands” at Tijuana Slough
events.description: Celebrate Latino Conservation Week with a free, family-friendly event featuring bilingual nature walks, birdwatching, hands-on wetland activities, arts and crafts, and opportunities to connect with local conservation experts and community partners. Presented by San Diego Bird Alliance in collaboration with The Nat, U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service, the Hispanic Access Foundation, and local conservation partners, Latino Conservation Week is an annual celebration highlighting the important role the Latinx community plays in enjoying, protecting, and caring for our region’s natural resources. Participants can explore the wetlands through bilingual guided walks, birdwatching, nature talks, hands-on activities, arts and crafts, and interactive science experiences. From discovering the tiny creatures living in the water to learning about the plants and birds that depend on the estuary, there will be something for every age and interest. One of the highlights will be a hands-on experience in the estuary, where participants can help plant 50 native plants, take part in a water quality demonstration, and spend time with biologists. Local conservation experts will help participants understand what these activities reveal about the health and importance of our wetlands. Families can also explore local biodiversity using iNaturalist, connect with conservation organizations, and discover nature up close through specimens, microscopes, field guides, and other educational tools. Latino Conservation Week is more than a celebration of nature. It is a celebration of community, culture, and collective action. See more details and register here . ¡Evento comunitario gratuito para todos! Free community event for all! For more information, please contact: Kornelas@sandiegobirdalliance.org
events.location: Tijuana Estuary Visitor Center, 301 Caspian Wy, Imperial Beach

events.title: Community Science Plastic Pellet (Nurdle) Cleanup 9/19/26
events.description: Join us at Rotary Park in Carlsbad for a community science plastic pellet (nurdle) cleanup. Plastic pellets are the building blocks of the plastic supply chain, making so many of the products we use in our daily lives — everything from milk jugs to plastic bags. Unfortunately, they are also entering our environment at staggering rates, with more than 10 trillion plastic pellets entering our oceans annually. We are planning to continually monitor this site and collect data to address and quantify plastic pellet pollution in our communities and treasured waterways. The California coast has seen plastic pellet pollution in recent years, and the data collected through pellet counts paves the way for lasting change. Where: Rotary Park, Carlsbad, CA 92008 Look for our blue banner table, located on the southeast side of the park, near Carlsbad Village Dr. 33°09'33.3″N 117°20'59.0″W When: 9 - 10 AM Note: Please wear comfortable clothes, closed-toed shoes, and sunscreen. All volunteers (individuals as well as groups) are welcome to participate and must sign a liability waiver. Volunteers under the age of 18 must have a parent or guardian present at the beginning of the cleanup to sign a liability waiver before the minor can participate. Register Here (capacity is limited)
